# Goal
Implement fa core **deadline awareness** for gh-1556 (acceptance criteria 5 & 6 of the ticket in input/gh-1556/ticket.md — read it first, sections "fa core (deadline awareness)" and "Threats / design notes"). This is the "temporal sibling of the FinalizeGate (gh-1412)".

# Repo conventions (MUST follow)
- Root is a pure-Dart package `flutter_agent_harness`: `lib/` core (NO `dart:io` anywhere in `lib/` — env/time IO only behind seams), `test/` mirrors `lib/`. Hosts/bin (`bin/`, `lib/src/cli/`) MAY use dart:io.
- God-file ceiling: no Dart file over 2800 lines; target < 2000 — split via `part` files using the established pattern when needed.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (gh-1232 policy): GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted within group; append only.
- Read AGENTS.md for more invariants before editing.
- TDD: write failing tests first in `test/` (never `testing/`).
- Do NOT touch: `bench/`, `.github/`, `docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `outputs/`. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT run the full test suite or formatters project-wide — run `dart analyze` scoped to changed files and your new/affected tests only.

# Feature spec (from the ticket)
**Deadline signal — three entry points, ONE clock:**
1. Hosts inject env var `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (epoch ms). Resolved LIVE per turn via the session-correlation env seam (same pattern as `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — a live provider consulted per call, so a mid-session `/timer` change is picked up immediately). The deadline should also be injected into bash tool executions through that seam (shell scripts see the current value).
2. CLI flag `fa --timer 25m` / `fa --deadline <duration|epoch>` — headless AND interactive; the flag just sets the same single session value.
3. TUI slash-command `/timer 25m` (set/adjust/clear mid-session; `/timer` with no arg shows the current value) + a countdown chip in the TUI status area while armed (pure projection of the one clock — no second timer source).

Absent/cleared deadline = today's behavior BYTE-FOR-BYTE (REG: prompt, session records, events unchanged — no extra lines anywhere).

**Budget surfacing + wrap-up steering:**
- Every LLM request context carries the remaining budget as a small per-turn line, e.g. `time-left: 5min`, refreshed per turn. Find the per-turn request/context build point (see `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` around the request construction, `systemPrompt:` usages) and inject there, ONLY when a deadline is armed.
- One-shot system notices at configured crossings, riding the existing `<system-notice>` machinery (see `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart` ~line 327 for the injection pattern and `lib/src/cli/system_notice_render.dart` / `lib/src/user_text.dart` for the envelope). Default ladder:
  - ~50% of budget elapsed: "half the budget gone" notice
  - T-3min (mandatory steer): "stop exploring, finalize outputs, drain/kill background jobs, run your checks" — the notice MUST name the shell-job/background-work drain explicitly (long-running operations must get their chance to land)
  - T-30s: "write final answer NOW"
  Each crossing fires ONCE per arming (reset when the deadline is re-set/adjusted). Notices are steerings — the model may ignore them; the guillotine stays the host's.
- Headless `fa -p` behavior: the wrap-up steering applies there too; when no deadline is set, headless exit behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Threats/design notes (binding):**
- Never lie about the clock: the deadline comes ONLY from host env / explicit user set; fa never invents or extends it; missing/invalid = feature off (silent, no errors).
- Not a procrastination loop: notices fire once per crossing.
- One clock, three setters; later setters override earlier; TUI chip is a pure projection.
- Suggested new module: pure-Dart `SessionDeadline` (e.g. `lib/src/session/session_deadline.dart`) holding the single epoch-ms value with an injectable clock (`DateTime Function()` defaulting to DateTime.now), set/clear/remaining, crossing state machine, and the `time-left:` formatter. Wire it in the CLI host (env read at boot + live seam provider + flag + slash command + status chip).

# Key files to study
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — env seam pattern
- `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart`, `bin/fah.dart` — CLI flag parsing
- `lib/src/cli/slash_menu.dart` (`builtinSlashCommands`), `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart` — slash dispatch
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart` — system prompt composition (`_applyPromptComposition`)
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — per-turn request building
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`, `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart` — status area/chip
- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart` — headless run
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the gh-1412 precedent this mirrors

# Acceptance criteria for YOUR part
- [ ] `SessionDeadline` pure-Dart module with injectable clock; invalid/missing env → off, silent
- [ ] All three entry points write the same session value with override order env < flag < live `/timer` adjustment (later wins)
- [ ] Per-turn `time-left:` line in LLM context only when armed; absent when not (byte-for-byte REG)
- [ ] One-shot crossing notices (50%, T-3min drain steer, T-30s) with fake-clock + scripted-loop tests proving once-only semantics
- [ ] TUI `/timer` command + countdown chip render test
- [ ] Headless flag works; deadline-unset headless byte-for-byte
- [ ] Duration parsing: `25m`, `90s`, `1h30m`, plain epoch-ms integer; invalid → clear error message (user-facing), never a silent wrong deadline
- [ ] `dart analyze` clean on changed files; all new + touched tests pass (`dart test <files>`)
- [ ] Barrel export appended per gh-1232 policy

Final message: report files created/modified, test commands + results, any seams you chose and why, and anything left unverified.

data.context:
# Goal
Implement fa core **deadline awareness** for gh-1556 (acceptance criteria 5 & 6 of the ticket in input/gh-1556/ticket.md — read it first, sections "fa core (deadline awareness)" and "Threats / design notes"). This is the "temporal sibling of the FinalizeGate (gh-1412)".

# Repo conventions (MUST follow)
- Root is a pure-Dart package `flutter_agent_harness`: `lib/` core (NO `dart:io` anywhere in `lib/` — env/time IO only behind seams), `test/` mirrors `lib/`. Hosts/bin (`bin/`, `lib/src/cli/`) MAY use dart:io.
- God-file ceiling: no Dart file over 2800 lines; target < 2000 — split via `part` files using the established pattern when needed.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (gh-1232 policy): GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted within group; append only.
- Read AGENTS.md for more invariants before editing.
- TDD: write failing tests first in `test/` (never `testing/`).
- Do NOT touch: `bench/`, `.github/`, `docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `outputs/`. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT run the full test suite or formatters project-wide — run `dart analyze` scoped to changed files and your new/affected tests only.

# Feature spec (from the ticket)
**Deadline signal — three entry points, ONE clock:**
1. Hosts inject env var `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (epoch ms). Resolved LIVE per turn via the session-correlation env seam (same pattern as `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — a live provider consulted per call, so a mid-session `/timer` change is picked up immediately). The deadline should also be injected into bash tool executions through that seam (shell scripts see the current value).
2. CLI flag `fa --timer 25m` / `fa --deadline <duration|epoch>` — headless AND interactive; the flag just sets the same single session value.
3. TUI slash-command `/timer 25m` (set/adjust/clear mid-session; `/timer` with no arg shows the current value) + a countdown chip in the TUI status area while armed (pure projection of the one clock — no second timer source).

Absent/cleared deadline = today's behavior BYTE-FOR-BYTE (REG: prompt, session records, events unchanged — no extra lines anywhere).

**Budget surfacing + wrap-up steering:**
- Every LLM request context carries the remaining budget as a small per-turn line, e.g. `time-left: 5min`, refreshed per turn. Find the per-turn request/context build point (see `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` around the request construction, `systemPrompt:` usages) and inject there, ONLY when a deadline is armed.
- One-shot system notices at configured crossings, riding the existing `<system-notice>` machinery (see `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart` ~line 327 for the injection pattern and `lib/src/cli/system_notice_render.dart` / `lib/src/user_text.dart` for the envelope). Default ladder:
  - ~50% of budget elapsed: "half the budget gone" notice
  - T-3min (mandatory steer): "stop exploring, finalize outputs, drain/kill background jobs, run your checks" — the notice MUST name the shell-job/background-work drain explicitly (long-running operations must get their chance to land)
  - T-30s: "write final answer NOW"
  Each crossing fires ONCE per arming (reset when the deadline is re-set/adjusted). Notices are steerings — the model may ignore them; the guillotine stays the host's.
- Headless `fa -p` behavior: the wrap-up steering applies there too; when no deadline is set, headless exit behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Threats/design notes (binding):**
- Never lie about the clock: the deadline comes ONLY from host env / explicit user set; fa never invents or extends it; missing/invalid = feature off (silent, no errors).
- Not a procrastination loop: notices fire once per crossing.
- One clock, three setters; later setters override earlier; TUI chip is a pure projection.
- Suggested new module: pure-Dart `SessionDeadline` (e.g. `lib/src/session/session_deadline.dart`) holding the single epoch-ms value with an injectable clock (`DateTime Function()` defaulting to DateTime.now), set/clear/remaining, crossing state machine, and the `time-left:` formatter. Wire it in the CLI host (env read at boot + live seam provider + flag + slash command + status chip).

# Key files to study
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — env seam pattern
- `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart`, `bin/fah.dart` — CLI flag parsing
- `lib/src/cli/slash_menu.dart` (`builtinSlashCommands`), `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart` — slash dispatch
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart` — system prompt composition (`_applyPromptComposition`)
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — per-turn request building
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`, `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart` — status area/chip
- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart` — headless run
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the gh-1412 precedent this mirrors

# Acceptance criteria for YOUR part
- [ ] `SessionDeadline` pure-Dart module with injectable clock; invalid/missing env → off, silent
- [ ] All three entry points write the same session value with override order env < flag < live `/timer` adjustment (later wins)
- [ ] Per-turn `time-left:` line in LLM context only when armed; absent when not (byte-for-byte REG)
- [ ] One-shot crossing notices (50%, T-3min drain steer, T-30s) with fake-clock + scripted-loop tests proving once-only semantics
- [ ] TUI `/timer` command + countdown chip render test
- [ ] Headless flag works; deadline-unset headless byte-for-byte
- [ ] Duration parsing: `25m`, `90s`, `1h30m`, plain epoch-ms integer; invalid → clear error message (user-facing), never a silent wrong deadline
- [ ] `dart analyze` clean on changed files; all new + touched tests pass (`dart test <files>`)
- [ ] Barrel export appended per gh-1232 policy

Final message: report files created/modified, test commands + results, any seams you chose and why, and anything left unverified.

data.context:
# Goal
Implement fa core **deadline awareness** for gh-1556 (acceptance criteria 5 & 6 of the ticket in input/gh-1556/ticket.md — read it first, sections "fa core (deadline awareness)" and "Threats / design notes"). This is the "temporal sibling of the FinalizeGate (gh-1412)".

# Repo conventions (MUST follow)
- Root is a pure-Dart package `flutter_agent_harness`: `lib/` core (NO `dart:io` anywhere in `lib/` — env/time IO only behind seams), `test/` mirrors `lib/`. Hosts/bin (`bin/`, `lib/src/cli/`) MAY use dart:io.
- God-file ceiling: no Dart file over 2800 lines; target < 2000 — split via `part` files using the established pattern when needed.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (gh-1232 policy): GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted within group; append only.
- Read AGENTS.md for more invariants before editing.
- TDD: write failing tests first in `test/` (never `testing/`).
- Do NOT touch: `bench/`, `.github/`, `docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `outputs/`. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT run the full test suite or formatters project-wide — run `dart analyze` scoped to changed files and your new/affected tests only.

# Feature spec (from the ticket)
**Deadline signal — three entry points, ONE clock:**
1. Hosts inject env var `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (epoch ms). Resolved LIVE per turn via the session-correlation env seam (same pattern as `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — a live provider consulted per call, so a mid-session `/timer` change is picked up immediately). The deadline should also be injected into bash tool executions through that seam (shell scripts see the current value).
2. CLI flag `fa --timer 25m` / `fa --deadline <duration|epoch>` — headless AND interactive; the flag just sets the same single session value.
3. TUI slash-command `/timer 25m` (set/adjust/clear mid-session; `/timer` with no arg shows the current value) + a countdown chip in the TUI status area while armed (pure projection of the one clock — no second timer source).

Absent/cleared deadline = today's behavior BYTE-FOR-BYTE (REG: prompt, session records, events unchanged — no extra lines anywhere).

**Budget surfacing + wrap-up steering:**
- Every LLM request context carries the remaining budget as a small per-turn line, e.g. `time-left: 5min`, refreshed per turn. Find the per-turn request/context build point (see `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` around the request construction, `systemPrompt:` usages) and inject there, ONLY when a deadline is armed.
- One-shot system notices at configured crossings, riding the existing `<system-notice>` machinery (see `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart` ~line 327 for the injection pattern and `lib/src/cli/system_notice_render.dart` / `lib/src/user_text.dart` for the envelope). Default ladder:
  - ~50% of budget elapsed: "half the budget gone" notice
  - T-3min (mandatory steer): "stop exploring, finalize outputs, drain/kill background jobs, run your checks" — the notice MUST name the shell-job/background-work drain explicitly (long-running operations must get their chance to land)
  - T-30s: "write final answer NOW"
  Each crossing fires ONCE per arming (reset when the deadline is re-set/adjusted). Notices are steerings — the model may ignore them; the guillotine stays the host's.
- Headless `fa -p` behavior: the wrap-up steering applies there too; when no deadline is set, headless exit behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Threats/design notes (binding):**
- Never lie about the clock: the deadline comes ONLY from host env / explicit user set; fa never invents or extends it; missing/invalid = feature off (silent, no errors).
- Not a procrastination loop: notices fire once per crossing.
- One clock, three setters; later setters override earlier; TUI chip is a pure projection.
- Suggested new module: pure-Dart `SessionDeadline` (e.g. `lib/src/session/session_deadline.dart`) holding the single epoch-ms value with an injectable clock (`DateTime Function()` defaulting to DateTime.now), set/clear/remaining, crossing state machine, and the `time-left:` formatter. Wire it in the CLI host (env read at boot + live seam provider + flag + slash command + status chip).

# Key files to study
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — env seam pattern
- `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart`, `bin/fah.dart` — CLI flag parsing
- `lib/src/cli/slash_menu.dart` (`builtinSlashCommands`), `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart` — slash dispatch
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart` — system prompt composition (`_applyPromptComposition`)
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — per-turn request building
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`, `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart` — status area/chip
- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart` — headless run
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the gh-1412 precedent this mirrors

# Acceptance criteria for YOUR part
- [ ] `SessionDeadline` pure-Dart module with injectable clock; invalid/missing env → off, silent
- [ ] All three entry points write the same session value with override order env < flag < live `/timer` adjustment (later wins)
- [ ] Per-turn `time-left:` line in LLM context only when armed; absent when not (byte-for-byte REG)
- [ ] One-shot crossing notices (50%, T-3min drain steer, T-30s) with fake-clock + scripted-loop tests proving once-only semantics
- [ ] TUI `/timer` command + countdown chip render test
- [ ] Headless flag works; deadline-unset headless byte-for-byte
- [ ] Duration parsing: `25m`, `90s`, `1h30m`, plain epoch-ms integer; invalid → clear error message (user-facing), never a silent wrong deadline
- [ ] `dart analyze` clean on changed files; all new + touched tests pass (`dart test <files>`)
- [ ] Barrel export appended per gh-1232 policy

Final message: report files created/modified, test commands + results, any seams you chose and why, and anything left unverified.

data.context:
# Goal
Implement fa core **deadline awareness** for gh-1556 (acceptance criteria 5 & 6 of the ticket in input/gh-1556/ticket.md — read it first, sections "fa core (deadline awareness)" and "Threats / design notes"). This is the "temporal sibling of the FinalizeGate (gh-1412)".

# Repo conventions (MUST follow)
- Root is a pure-Dart package `flutter_agent_harness`: `lib/` core (NO `dart:io` anywhere in `lib/` — env/time IO only behind seams), `test/` mirrors `lib/`. Hosts/bin (`bin/`, `lib/src/cli/`) MAY use dart:io.
- God-file ceiling: no Dart file over 2800 lines; target < 2000 — split via `part` files using the established pattern when needed.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (gh-1232 policy): GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted within group; append only.
- Read AGENTS.md for more invariants before editing.
- TDD: write failing tests first in `test/` (never `testing/`).
- Do NOT touch: `bench/`, `.github/`, `docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `outputs/`. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT run the full test suite or formatters project-wide — run `dart analyze` scoped to changed files and your new/affected tests only.

# Feature spec (from the ticket)
**Deadline signal — three entry points, ONE clock:**
1. Hosts inject env var `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (epoch ms). Resolved LIVE per turn via the session-correlation env seam (same pattern as `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — a live provider consulted per call, so a mid-session `/timer` change is picked up immediately). The deadline should also be injected into bash tool executions through that seam (shell scripts see the current value).
2. CLI flag `fa --timer 25m` / `fa --deadline <duration|epoch>` — headless AND interactive; the flag just sets the same single session value.
3. TUI slash-command `/timer 25m` (set/adjust/clear mid-session; `/timer` with no arg shows the current value) + a countdown chip in the TUI status area while armed (pure projection of the one clock — no second timer source).

Absent/cleared deadline = today's behavior BYTE-FOR-BYTE (REG: prompt, session records, events unchanged — no extra lines anywhere).

**Budget surfacing + wrap-up steering:**
- Every LLM request context carries the remaining budget as a small per-turn line, e.g. `time-left: 5min`, refreshed per turn. Find the per-turn request/context build point (see `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` around the request construction, `systemPrompt:` usages) and inject there, ONLY when a deadline is armed.
- One-shot system notices at configured crossings, riding the existing `<system-notice>` machinery (see `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart` ~line 327 for the injection pattern and `lib/src/cli/system_notice_render.dart` / `lib/src/user_text.dart` for the envelope). Default ladder:
  - ~50% of budget elapsed: "half the budget gone" notice
  - T-3min (mandatory steer): "stop exploring, finalize outputs, drain/kill background jobs, run your checks" — the notice MUST name the shell-job/background-work drain explicitly (long-running operations must get their chance to land)
  - T-30s: "write final answer NOW"
  Each crossing fires ONCE per arming (reset when the deadline is re-set/adjusted). Notices are steerings — the model may ignore them; the guillotine stays the host's.
- Headless `fa -p` behavior: the wrap-up steering applies there too; when no deadline is set, headless exit behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Threats/design notes (binding):**
- Never lie about the clock: the deadline comes ONLY from host env / explicit user set; fa never invents or extends it; missing/invalid = feature off (silent, no errors).
- Not a procrastination loop: notices fire once per crossing.
- One clock, three setters; later setters override earlier; TUI chip is a pure projection.
- Suggested new module: pure-Dart `SessionDeadline` (e.g. `lib/src/session/session_deadline.dart`) holding the single epoch-ms value with an injectable clock (`DateTime Function()` defaulting to DateTime.now), set/clear/remaining, crossing state machine, and the `time-left:` formatter. Wire it in the CLI host (env read at boot + live seam provider + flag + slash command + status chip).

# Key files to study
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — env seam pattern
- `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart`, `bin/fah.dart` — CLI flag parsing
- `lib/src/cli/slash_menu.dart` (`builtinSlashCommands`), `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart` — slash dispatch
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart` — system prompt composition (`_applyPromptComposition`)
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — per-turn request building
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`, `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart` — status area/chip
- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart` — headless run
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the gh-1412 precedent this mirrors

# Acceptance criteria for YOUR part
- [ ] `SessionDeadline` pure-Dart module with injectable clock; invalid/missing env → off, silent
- [ ] All three entry points write the same session value with override order env < flag < live `/timer` adjustment (later wins)
- [ ] Per-turn `time-left:` line in LLM context only when armed; absent when not (byte-for-byte REG)
- [ ] One-shot crossing notices (50%, T-3min drain steer, T-30s) with fake-clock + scripted-loop tests proving once-only semantics
- [ ] TUI `/timer` command + countdown chip render test
- [ ] Headless flag works; deadline-unset headless byte-for-byte
- [ ] Duration parsing: `25m`, `90s`, `1h30m`, plain epoch-ms integer; invalid → clear error message (user-facing), never a silent wrong deadline
- [ ] `dart analyze` clean on changed files; all new + touched tests pass (`dart test <files>`)
- [ ] Barrel export appended per gh-1232 policy

Final message: report files created/modified, test commands + results, any seams you chose and why, and anything left unverified.

data.context:
# Goal
Implement fa core **deadline awareness** for gh-1556 (acceptance criteria 5 & 6 of the ticket in input/gh-1556/ticket.md — read it first, sections "fa core (deadline awareness)" and "Threats / design notes"). This is the "temporal sibling of the FinalizeGate (gh-1412)".

# Repo conventions (MUST follow)
- Root is a pure-Dart package `flutter_agent_harness`: `lib/` core (NO `dart:io` anywhere in `lib/` — env/time IO only behind seams), `test/` mirrors `lib/`. Hosts/bin (`bin/`, `lib/src/cli/`) MAY use dart:io.
- God-file ceiling: no Dart file over 2800 lines; target < 2000 — split via `part` files using the established pattern when needed.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (gh-1232 policy): GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted within group; append only.
- Read AGENTS.md for more invariants before editing.
- TDD: write failing tests first in `test/` (never `testing/`).
- Do NOT touch: `bench/`, `.github/`, `docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `outputs/`. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT run the full test suite or formatters project-wide — run `dart analyze` scoped to changed files and your new/affected tests only.

# Feature spec (from the ticket)
**Deadline signal — three entry points, ONE clock:**
1. Hosts inject env var `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (epoch ms). Resolved LIVE per turn via the session-correlation env seam (same pattern as `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — a live provider consulted per call, so a mid-session `/timer` change is picked up immediately). The deadline should also be injected into bash tool executions through that seam (shell scripts see the current value).
2. CLI flag `fa --timer 25m` / `fa --deadline <duration|epoch>` — headless AND interactive; the flag just sets the same single session value.
3. TUI slash-command `/timer 25m` (set/adjust/clear mid-session; `/timer` with no arg shows the current value) + a countdown chip in the TUI status area while armed (pure projection of the one clock — no second timer source).

Absent/cleared deadline = today's behavior BYTE-FOR-BYTE (REG: prompt, session records, events unchanged — no extra lines anywhere).

**Budget surfacing + wrap-up steering:**
- Every LLM request context carries the remaining budget as a small per-turn line, e.g. `time-left: 5min`, refreshed per turn. Find the per-turn request/context build point (see `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` around the request construction, `systemPrompt:` usages) and inject there, ONLY when a deadline is armed.
- One-shot system notices at configured crossings, riding the existing `<system-notice>` machinery (see `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart` ~line 327 for the injection pattern and `lib/src/cli/system_notice_render.dart` / `lib/src/user_text.dart` for the envelope). Default ladder:
  - ~50% of budget elapsed: "half the budget gone" notice
  - T-3min (mandatory steer): "stop exploring, finalize outputs, drain/kill background jobs, run your checks" — the notice MUST name the shell-job/background-work drain explicitly (long-running operations must get their chance to land)
  - T-30s: "write final answer NOW"
  Each crossing fires ONCE per arming (reset when the deadline is re-set/adjusted). Notices are steerings — the model may ignore them; the guillotine stays the host's.
- Headless `fa -p` behavior: the wrap-up steering applies there too; when no deadline is set, headless exit behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Threats/design notes (binding):**
- Never lie about the clock: the deadline comes ONLY from host env / explicit user set; fa never invents or extends it; missing/invalid = feature off (silent, no errors).
- Not a procrastination loop: notices fire once per crossing.
- One clock, three setters; later setters override earlier; TUI chip is a pure projection.
- Suggested new module: pure-Dart `SessionDeadline` (e.g. `lib/src/session/session_deadline.dart`) holding the single epoch-ms value with an injectable clock (`DateTime Function()` defaulting to DateTime.now), set/clear/remaining, crossing state machine, and the `time-left:` formatter. Wire it in the CLI host (env read at boot + live seam provider + flag + slash command + status chip).

# Key files to study
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — env seam pattern
- `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart`, `bin/fah.dart` — CLI flag parsing
- `lib/src/cli/slash_menu.dart` (`builtinSlashCommands`), `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart` — slash dispatch
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart` — system prompt composition (`_applyPromptComposition`)
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — per-turn request building
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`, `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart` — status area/chip
- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart` — headless run
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the gh-1412 precedent this mirrors

# Acceptance criteria for YOUR part
- [ ] `SessionDeadline` pure-Dart module with injectable clock; invalid/missing env → off, silent
- [ ] All three entry points write the same session value with override order env < flag < live `/timer` adjustment (later wins)
- [ ] Per-turn `time-left:` line in LLM context only when armed; absent when not (byte-for-byte REG)
- [ ] One-shot crossing notices (50%, T-3min drain steer, T-30s) with fake-clock + scripted-loop tests proving once-only semantics
- [ ] TUI `/timer` command + countdown chip render test
- [ ] Headless flag works; deadline-unset headless byte-for-byte
- [ ] Duration parsing: `25m`, `90s`, `1h30m`, plain epoch-ms integer; invalid → clear error message (user-facing), never a silent wrong deadline
- [ ] `dart analyze` clean on changed files; all new + touched tests pass (`dart test <files>`)
- [ ] Barrel export appended per gh-1232 policy

Final message: report files created/modified, test commands + results, any seams you chose and why, and anything left unverified.

Implement fa core **deadline awareness** for gh-1556 (acceptance criteria 5 & 6 of the ticket in input/gh-1556/ticket.md — read it first, sections "fa core (deadline awareness)" and "Threats / design notes"). This is the "temporal sibling of the FinalizeGate (gh-1412)".

# Repo conventions (MUST follow)
- Root is a pure-Dart package `flutter_agent_harness`: `lib/` core (NO `dart:io` anywhere in `lib/` — env/time IO only behind seams), `test/` mirrors `lib/`. Hosts/bin (`bin/`, `lib/src/cli/`) MAY use dart:io.
- God-file ceiling: no Dart file over 2800 lines; target < 2000 — split via `part` files using the established pattern when needed.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (gh-1232 policy): GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted within group; append only.
- Read AGENTS.md for more invariants before editing.
- TDD: write failing tests first in `test/` (never `testing/`).
- Do NOT touch: `bench/`, `.github/`, `docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `outputs/`. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT run the full test suite or formatters project-wide — run `dart analyze` scoped to changed files and your new/affected tests only.

# Feature spec (from the ticket)
**Deadline signal — three entry points, ONE clock:**
1. Hosts inject env var `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (epoch ms). Resolved LIVE per turn via the session-correlation env seam (same pattern as `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — a live provider consulted per call, so a mid-session `/timer` change is picked up immediately). The deadline should also be injected into bash tool executions through that seam (shell scripts see the current value).
2. CLI flag `fa --timer 25m` / `fa --deadline <duration|epoch>` — headless AND interactive; the flag just sets the same single session value.
3. TUI slash-command `/timer 25m` (set/adjust/clear mid-session; `/timer` with no arg shows the current value) + a countdown chip in the TUI status area while armed (pure projection of the one clock — no second timer source).

Absent/cleared deadline = today's behavior BYTE-FOR-BYTE (REG: prompt, session records, events unchanged — no extra lines anywhere).

**Budget surfacing + wrap-up steering:**
- Every LLM request context carries the remaining budget as a small per-turn line, e.g. `time-left: 5min`, refreshed per turn. Find the per-turn request/context build point (see `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` around the request construction, `systemPrompt:` usages) and inject there, ONLY when a deadline is armed.
- One-shot system notices at configured crossings, riding the existing `<system-notice>` machinery (see `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart` ~line 327 for the injection pattern and `lib/src/cli/system_notice_render.dart` / `lib/src/user_text.dart` for the envelope). Default ladder:
  - ~50% of budget elapsed: "half the budget gone" notice
  - T-3min (mandatory steer): "stop exploring, finalize outputs, drain/kill background jobs, run your checks" — the notice MUST name the shell-job/background-work drain explicitly (long-running operations must get their chance to land)
  - T-30s: "write final answer NOW"
  Each crossing fires ONCE per arming (reset when the deadline is re-set/adjusted). Notices are steerings — the model may ignore them; the guillotine stays the host's.
- Headless `fa -p` behavior: the wrap-up steering applies there too; when no deadline is set, headless exit behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Threats/design notes (binding):**
- Never lie about the clock: the deadline comes ONLY from host env / explicit user set; fa never invents or extends it; missing/invalid = feature off (silent, no errors).
- Not a procrastination loop: notices fire once per crossing.
- One clock, three setters; later setters override earlier; TUI chip is a pure projection.
- Suggested new module: pure-Dart `SessionDeadline` (e.g. `lib/src/session/session_deadline.dart`) holding the single epoch-ms value with an injectable clock (`DateTime Function()` defaulting to DateTime.now), set/clear/remaining, crossing state machine, and the `time-left:` formatter. Wire it in the CLI host (env read at boot + live seam provider + flag + slash command + status chip).

# Key files to study
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — env seam pattern
- `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart`, `bin/fah.dart` — CLI flag parsing
- `lib/src/cli/slash_menu.dart` (`builtinSlashCommands`), `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_commands.dart` — slash dispatch
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart` — system prompt composition (`_applyPromptComposition`)
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — per-turn request building
- `lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart`, `lib/src/cli/tui_status_line.dart` — status area/chip
- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_run.dart` — headless run
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the gh-1412 precedent this mirrors

# Acceptance criteria for YOUR part
- [ ] `SessionDeadline` pure-Dart module with injectable clock; invalid/missing env → off, silent
- [ ] All three entry points write the same session value with override order env < flag < live `/timer` adjustment (later wins)
- [ ] Per-turn `time-left:` line in LLM context only when armed; absent when not (byte-for-byte REG)
- [ ] One-shot crossing notices (50%, T-3min drain steer, T-30s) with fake-clock + scripted-loop tests proving once-only semantics
- [ ] TUI `/timer` command + countdown chip render test
- [ ] Headless flag works; deadline-unset headless byte-for-byte
- [ ] Duration parsing: `25m`, `90s`, `1h30m`, plain epoch-ms integer; invalid → clear error message (user-facing), never a silent wrong deadline
- [ ] `dart analyze` clean on changed files; all new + touched tests pass (`dart test <files>`)
- [ ] Barrel export appended per gh-1232 policy

Final message: report files created/modified, test commands + results, any seams you chose and why, and anything left unverified.

Hosts inject `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (epoch ms; resolved live per turn through the session-correlation seam above, so a mid-session `/timer` change reaches the next bash exec and the next LLM request); `fa --timer 25m` / `--deadline <duration|epoch>` (headless AND interactive) and the TUI `/timer` slash-command write the same single session value (env < flag < `/timer`; later wins). Missing/invalid env = feature off, byte-for-byte today's behavior; an explicit invalid user spec is a clear `FormatException`, never a silent wrong clock. Wired around `builtinTools` in `AgentCli` + `AgentService`. `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment` (never replaces).
- `lib/src/env/memory_execution_env.dart` — `MemoryExecutionEnv`: pure-Dart in-memory `ExecutionEnv` (POSIX `/`-paths, default `Shell = UnavailableShell` reporting `shellUnavailable`). Default for tests and web consumers; shell-backed variants use `LocalShell` instead.

- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`: `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting `FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL` (resolved live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash. Wired around `builtinTools` in `AgentCli` + `AgentService`. `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment` (never replaces).
- `lib/src/env/memory_execution_env.dart` — `MemoryExecutionEnv`: pure-Dart in-memory `ExecutionEnv` (POSIX `/`-paths, default `Shell = UnavailableShell` reporting `shellUnavailable`). Default for tests and web consumers; shell-backed variants use `LocalShell` instead.

- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`: `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting `FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL` (resolved live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash. Wired around `builtinTools` in `AgentCli` + `AgentService`. `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment` (never replaces).
- `lib/src/env/memory_execution_env.dart` — `MemoryExecutionEnv`: pure-Dart in-memory `ExecutionEnv` (POSIX `/`-paths, default `Shell = UnavailableShell` reporting `shellUnavailable`). Default for tests and web consumers; shell-backed variants use `LocalShell` instead.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools for context hygiene. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` + `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree navigation). Summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.

- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` + `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree navigation). Summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.

    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only

    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need

    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with

    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.

    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.

    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a

    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:

    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:

  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with

    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart
