tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new

    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task

    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only

    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded

    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty

    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are

    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open

    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need

    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf

    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic

    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),

    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the

  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only

    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.

  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the

  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf

    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the

  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only

    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task

    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only

  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need

    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:

  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with

    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed

arguments.content:
### What changed
Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

### Key decisions
- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.
- The harbor deadline is stashed once at run start so the exported env value and the `fa-timeout-metadata.json` audit field are identical.
- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.
- `SessionDeadline` reuses the existing `SessionVarsExecutionEnv` seam (live per exec) rather than adding a second env provider.
- AC9 (no full 2.1 dispatch before a green smoke) is a process gate, not code — documented in `docs/bench.md`.

### How to verify
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 356 ok
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa        # 77 ok
dart analyze                                           # 0 errors/warnings
dart test test/session_deadline_test.dart test/agent/session_deadline_loop_test.dart \
  test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart                   # 32/32
```
Full `dart test` note: the monolithic run passed 7448 tests but the runner's Dart VM aborted twice with a native `malloc_consolidate` crash under sustained load; all 22 recorded failures are ambient-env leaks (`FA_LOG_FILE`/`FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` exported by the dev-runner harness) or load flakes — every failing file re-runs green individually with a sanitized env (incl. `origin/main` failing the boot-perf test identically here).

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  ENV[FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS host env] --> SD[SessionDeadline — one clock]
  FLAG[fa --timer/--deadline] --> SD
  SLASH[TUI /timer] --> SD
  SD --> CTX[per-turn time-left: request line]
  SD --> NOTICE[one-shot system notices 50% / T-3min / T-30s]
  SD --> CHIP[TUI countdown chip — pure projection]
  SD --> BASH[bash env via SessionVarsExecutionEnv — live per exec]
  CAP[adapter effective kill cap] --> DEADLINE[FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS = cap − 120s]
  DEADLINE --> ENV
```
</details>

{"content":"### What changed
Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

### Key decisions
- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.
- The harbor deadline is stashed once at run start so the exported env value and the `fa-timeout-metadata.json` audit field are identical.
- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.
- `SessionDeadline` reuses the existing `SessionVarsExecutionEnv` seam (live per exec) rather than adding a second env provider.
- AC9 (no full 2.1 dispatch before a green smoke) is a process gate, not code — documented in `docs/bench.md`.

### How to verify
```bash

python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa        # 77 ok

- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.

{"content":"### What changed
Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

### Key decisions
- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.
- The harbor deadline is stashed once at run start so the exported env value and the `fa-timeout-metadata.json` audit field are identical.
- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.
- `SessionDeadline` reuses the existing `SessionVarsExecutionEnv` seam (live per exec) rather than adding a second env provider.
- AC9 (no full 2.1 dispatch before a green smoke) is a process gate, not code — documented in `docs/bench.md`.

Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. ### Key decisions

Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

### Key decisions
- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.
- The harbor deadline is stashed once at run start so the exported env value and the `fa-timeout-metadata.json` audit field are identical.
- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.
- `SessionDeadline` reuses the existing `SessionVarsExecutionEnv` seam (live per exec) rather than adding a second env provider.

{"content":"### What changed
Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

### Key decisions
- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.
- The harbor deadline is stashed once at run start so the exported env value and the `fa-timeout-metadata.json` audit field are identical.
- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.
- `SessionDeadline` reuses the existing `SessionVarsExecutionEnv` seam (live per exec) rather than adding a second env provider.
- AC9 (no full 2.1 dispatch before a green smoke) is a process gate, not code — documented in `docs/bench.md`.

### How to verify
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 356 ok
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa        # 77 ok
dart analyze                                           # 0 errors/warnings
dart test test/session_deadline_test.dart test/agent/session_deadline_loop_test.dart \
  test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart                   # 32/32
```
Full `dart test` note: the monolithic run passed 7448 tests but the runner's Dart VM aborted twice with a native `malloc_consolidate` crash under sustained load; all 22 recorded failures are ambient-env leaks (`FA_LOG_FILE`/`FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` exported by the dev-runner harness) or load flakes — every failing file re-runs green individually with a sanitized env (incl. `origin/main` failing the boot-perf test identically here).

flowchart TD

  SD --> NOTICE[one-shot system notices 50% / T-3min / T-30s]
  SD --> CHIP[TUI countdown chip — pure projection]
  SD --> BASH[bash env via SessionVarsExecutionEnv — live per exec]
  CAP[adapter effective kill cap] --> DEADLINE[FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS = cap − 120s]
  DEADLINE --> ENV
```
</details>

Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

### Key decisions
- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.

- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.
- `SessionDeadline` reuses the existing `SessionVarsExecutionEnv` seam (live per exec) rather than adding a second env provider.

{"content":"### What changed
Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

### Key decisions
- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.
- The harbor deadline is stashed once at run start so the exported env value and the `fa-timeout-metadata.json` audit field are identical.
- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.
- `SessionDeadline` reuses the existing `SessionVarsExecutionEnv` seam (live per exec) rather than adding a second env provider.
- AC9 (no full 2.1 dispatch before a green smoke) is a process gate, not code — documented in `docs/bench.md`.

```bash

python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa        # 77 ok

{"content":"### What changed
Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

### Key decisions
- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.
- The harbor deadline is stashed once at run start so the exported env value and the `fa-timeout-metadata.json` audit field are identical.
- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.
- `SessionDeadline` reuses the existing `SessionVarsExecutionEnv` seam (live per exec) rather than adding a second env provider.
- AC9 (no full 2.1 dispatch before a green smoke) is a process gate, not code — documented in `docs/bench.md`.

Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

### Key decisions
- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.

- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.
- `SessionDeadline` reuses the existing `SessionVarsExecutionEnv` seam (live per exec) rather than adding a second env provider.

Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.

- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.

- **AC2 progress-watch default**: `bench-harbor.yml` exports `FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1`, `FA_STALL_GAP_SEC=360` (gh-1430 watchdog invariant), `FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC=3600` on every shard; the harbor adapter now selects the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` in watch mode (parity with the tb adapter) — legacy ladder stays byte-for-byte reachable by knob removal.

## fa core (Dart, via subagent + my review)
- `lib/src/session_deadline.dart`: one clock, three setters (env < flag < `/timer`), injectable clock, once-only crossing notices (50% / T-3min drain steer / T-30s), invalid env silent-off, invalid user spec loud.
